# Syntyr CSS — consolidated public reference

Source-tree version: 0.3.0-alpha.5 (may be an unreleased candidate).
Published immutable release: 0.3.0-alpha.4.

WARNING: This reference follows repository source. Before generating markup,
check the installed release and CSS modules. Do not assume alpha.5 features
exist in the published alpha.4 release. Syntyr is CSS, not a JS widget library.

Generated from an explicit allowlist by scripts/build_agent_docs.py.
Do not edit this file directly.
Relative links below are relative to each original source file, not this combined file.

## Source: docs/ai-quickstart.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/ai-quickstart.md

# Syntyr CSS: AI-agent quickstart

Use this guide when creating an application **with** Syntyr. To modify Syntyr itself, also read the repository [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/AGENTS.md). Syntyr supplies styles, **not** application logic or a JavaScript component system.

## 1. Choose the correct version

| Version | Status | Themes | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0.3.0-alpha.4` | Published immutable release | `grid`, `noir`, `studio` | Safe to pin for examples below |
| `0.3.0-alpha.5` | Unreleased source candidate | Seven themes including `industrial`, `terminal`, `corporate`, `minimal` | Do not cite as a downloadable tagged release |

For a production application, copy a tagged CSS release to your own origin and pin its version. The CDN URL below is suitable for an initial prototype:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/v/0.3.0-alpha.4/syntyr.core.css">
```

For page-level recipes, load the same **version** of the optional module after core:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/v/0.3.0-alpha.4/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/v/0.3.0-alpha.4/syntyr.recipes.css">
```

Do not combine `syntyr.all.css` with individual CSS modules; that loads duplicates. A stylesheet is not automatically installed by adding a `syn-*` class to markup.

## 2. Generate valid HTML

```html
<main class="syn-root syn-page" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <div class="syn-shell">
    <header class="syn-header">
      <a href="/" class="syn-logo">Acme</a>
      <nav aria-label="Primary navigation"><a href="/reports">Reports</a></nav>
    </header>
    <section class="syn-panel" aria-labelledby="reports-title">
      <h1 class="syn-heading" id="reports-title">Reports</h1>
      <p class="syn-muted">View recent activity.</p>
      <a class="syn-button syn-button--primary" href="/reports/new">New report</a>
    </section>
  </div>
</main>
```

All classes in this sample are available from published alpha.4 core. Use an `<a>` for navigation, a `<button>` for an action, and functional `href`/`action` values rather than dummy `#` placeholders.

## 3. Use responsive recipes only when their module is loaded

```html
<section class="syn-root syn-region" data-syn-theme="studio" aria-label="Operations overview">
  <div class="syn-stats">
    <article class="syn-stat">
      <p class="syn-stat-label">Open tickets</p>
      <p class="syn-stat-value">14</p>
    </article>
    <article class="syn-stat">
      <p class="syn-stat-label">Resolved today</p>
      <p class="syn-stat-value">8</p>
    </article>
  </div>
</section>
```

`syn-region` and `syn-stats` are core classes; they use native container queries. The containing region must be an ancestor of the responsive pattern. For application shells, `syn-app-shell` is in **recipes**, not core.

## 4. Optional scoped semantic mode

Load `syntyr.semantic.css` **after core**, then opt into `syn-semantic` in a `syn-root` subtree. Ordinary HTML outside that subtree is unaffected.

```html
<section class="syn-root syn-semantic" data-syn-theme="noir">
  <form action="/login" method="post">
    <label for="email">Email <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required></label>
    <button type="submit">Sign in</button>
  </form>
</section>
```

The form must have a real server handler. Syntyr does not provide authentication, CSRF protection, requests or validation logic.

## 5. Framework rules and accessibility

- **React/JSX:** use `className`, `htmlFor`, and normal framework event handlers. Syntyr styles HTML but does not expose React components.
- **HTMX/Datastar:** let the host library manage state and requests; preserve native form behavior. For transient class-changing elements inside semantic mode, see the [framework integration guide](framework-integrations.md) for `data-syn-semantic`.
- **Themes:** `data-syn-theme` belongs on `.syn-root` or a nested themed subtree. Prefer `studio` for professional SaaS, `grid`/`noir` for cinematic interfaces.
- **Accessibility:** preserve keyboard focus, form labels, descriptive error messages, link destinations and reduced-motion preferences. `aria-pressed` describes an actual pressed toggle; `aria-busy` alone does not perform loading.
- **Visualization:** `syntyr.viz.css` styles provided SVG and HTML. It **does not calculate chart geometry** or provide a renderer.
- **Custom theme:** override documented `--syn-*` variables in application CSS. Verify text/background and interactive contrast.

## 6. Verify generated output

1. Identify the installed Syntyr **version** and CSS modules.
2. Check every `syn-*` class against [components](components.md), [recipes](recipes.md), or the [validated curated manifest](../metadata/components.json).
3. Ensure the browser actually loads each required stylesheet, without duplicates.
4. Check interactive elements, keyboard navigation, high-zoom reflow and browser console.
5. Do not claim a static Syntyr example implements fetching, persistence, sorting, filtering or authentication.

See [agent integration](agent-integration.md) for reusable prompt instructions.

## Source: docs/components.md

# Syntyr CSS component and token contract

Status: **experimental v0.3-alpha**, not yet released to a package registry. All CSS and markup are original to this repository; no upstream source code was copied.

Native elements such as `search`, `figure`, `figcaption`, `kbd`, `mark`, `output`, `meter`, and `pre` are styled only in the optional semantic mode. See [the no-JS native example](../examples/native-elements.html). The regular component-class API and HTML outside `.syn-root` are unchanged.

## Loading and scoping

For the explicitly classed API (no automatic unclassed element styles):

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="syntyr.core.css">
<body class="syn-root syn-page" data-syn-theme="grid">
  <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary">Run</button>
</body>
```

For Pico-like semantic markup, add the optional file **after** core and mark the subtree. Unclassed elements style automatically; opt in class-changing elements with `data-syn-semantic`:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="syntyr.semantic.css">
<section class="syn-root syn-semantic" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <article>
    <label for="id">Operator <input id="id" name="id" required></label>
    <button data-syn-semantic>Continue</button>
  </article>
</section>
```

Class-based components, recipes, effects, and geometry apply only to elements
inside a Syntyr root, including classes attached directly to the root itself.
A bare Syntyr class on an unrelated host element is deliberately ignored, so
framework-owned components and existing application CSS are not restyled.
The root boundary is enforced through modern native CSS nesting with
a zero-specificity selector rather than a global reset. Checkboxes and
radio controls using the explicit styling API retain a minimum 24 CSS px box;
the surrounding label should provide additional activation area.

For optional effects, load `syntyr.effects.css`. `syntyr.css` is the convenient core + effects entry point. `syntyr.all.css` combines everything (semantic styling still requires `.syn-semantic`). `syn-root` should wrap any themed subtree; nested `data-syn-theme` overrides color tokens. The separate `data-syn-intensity="quiet|standard|cinematic"` attribute controls decorative strength on a root or nested region. Load `syntyr.geometry.css` for a `.syn-frame` with one shape and optional `.syn-frame--accent`. See the [visual-intensity guide](visual-intensity.md).

## Components

| Area | CSS API | Semantic alternative |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Buttons | `.syn-button`, `.syn-button--primary`, `.syn-button--outline`, `.syn-button--danger`, `.syn-button--small`, `.syn-button--ghost` | unclassed `button` |
| Panels | `.syn-panel`, `.syn-panel--cut` | unclassed `article` |
| Layout | `.syn-page` (viewport-height opt-in), `.syn-shell`, `.syn-header`, `.syn-grid`, `.syn-layout`, `.syn-inline`, `.syn-stack` | normal CSS layout |
| Typography | `.syn-logo`, `.syn-eyebrow`, `.syn-title`, `.syn-section-heading`, `.syn-heading`, `.syn-lede`, `.syn-mono`, `.syn-caption`, `.syn-muted` | native heading/text |
| Status | `.syn-badge`, `.syn-badge--accent`, `.syn-status` and semantic variants, `.syn-alert`, `.syn-alert--danger`, `.syn-meter` on `progress` | native `progress` |
| Forms | `.syn-form`, `.syn-label`, `.syn-input`, `.syn-select`, `.syn-textarea`, `.syn-check`, `.syn-fieldset`, `.syn-help`, `.syn-error` | unclassed form controls |
| Form compositions | `.syn-field`, `.syn-field-row`, `.syn-field-body`, `.syn-input-group`, `.syn-input-addon`, `.syn-error-summary` | native `form`, `label`, `input`, `button` |
| Overlays | `.syn-popover` on `[popover]`, `.syn-dialog` on `dialog`, `.syn-details` on `details` | browser defaults |
| Data | `.syn-table-wrap`, `.syn-table`, `.syn-cell--wrap`, `.syn-cell--numeric`, `.syn-description-list`, `.syn-description-actions` | unclassed `table`, native `dl` |
| Navigation | `.syn-breadcrumbs`, `.syn-pagination`, `.syn-page-link` | native `<nav>`, `<ol>`, links and `aria-current` |
| Loading | `.syn-skeleton`, `.syn-skeleton--short` | decorative placeholders; announce status separately |
| Effects (optional) | `.syn-grid-effect`, `.syn-glow`, `.syn-scanlines` | none |

### Optional composition utilities and component overrides

Load `syntyr.utilities.css` in addition to core to use finite helpers:
`syn-u-w-full`, `syn-u-max-reading`, `syn-u-overflow-auto`,
`syn-u-text-center`, `syn-u-min-w-0` and `syn-u-wrap`. These classes
work only inside `.syn-root` and do not require a class generator.
The existing flex/grid/spacing helpers are unchanged. Load the optional
module only when it is needed.

Customize individual components with custom properties rather than a new
set of modifiers:

```html
<article class="syn-panel"
         style="--syn-panel-padding:1.5rem; --syn-panel-radius:.75rem;
                --syn-panel-border-width:2px">
  <button class="syn-button"
          style="--syn-button-padding-inline:1.25rem;
                 --syn-button-border-width:2px">Open</button>
</article>
```

Defaults preserve the previous appearance: fluid panel padding, square
panel corners, and 1px borders; button inline padding defaults to 1rem.
These values are local CSS custom properties, not compile-time settings.
Inspect `metadata/syntyr-api.json` for the machine-readable API index,
or use the [editor integration instructions](editor-integration.md).

Use native button `popovertarget="id"` to control a popover and `commandfor="id" command="show-modal"` to open a dialog in supporting browsers. This last native dialog invoker API has newer browser support; provide alternate ways to reach important content where needed. Do not build custom ARIA dialog/tab/combobox patterns unless they are tested and necessary.

### Review screens and accessible error summaries

For server-rendered validation, combine `.syn-error-summary` with `.syn-error`, `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby`, and have the application move focus to the summary after a failed submit. For key/value review views, use a native `dl.syn-description-list` with `dt`/`dd` children. Table sort affordances respond to `th[aria-sort] > button`; the application supplies the sorting logic and updates `aria-sort`. The styles use logical direction where appropriate. See the [design-system pattern guide](mature-system-patterns.md) and [static example](../examples/mature-patterns.html).

## Neutral-first visual styling

The implicit `.syn-root` palette is Studio (light and sans-serif). Explicit `data-syn-theme="grid"` and `data-syn-theme="terminal"` retain technical monospace presentation; other themes remain opt-in. `.syn-panel` and `.syn-stage` are flat by default; add `syn-surface--accent` from the optional recipes CSS for emphasis, or the effects stylesheet for cinematic treatments. `.syn-badge` is a neutral label; use `.syn-status` with readable status text for meaningful state, or `.syn-badge--accent` to emphasize a badge.

Use `.syn-section-heading` between `.syn-heading` and `.syn-display`. Tables retain compact no-wrap defaults for identifiers and numeric values; add `.syn-cell--wrap` to descriptive cells. Selected rows have a logical inline-start accent border in addition to their fill. Keep wide tables in `.syn-table-wrap` and provide an accessible caption.

## Theme tokens

| Token | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `--syn-bg`, `--syn-surface`, `--syn-surface-hi` | Background surfaces |
| `--syn-text`, `--syn-muted` | Foreground text |
| `--syn-accent`, `--syn-on-accent`, `--syn-accent-soft` | Accent and contrast |
| `--syn-frame`, `--syn-danger` | Borders and warning states |
| `--syn-font`, `--syn-mono` | System typography |
| `--syn-space-1` ... `--syn-space-5` | Spacing scale |
| `--syn-cut`, `--syn-radius`, `--syn-line`, `--syn-control-height` | Shape and layout |

Application CSS can override tokens:

```css
/* Unlayered CSS overrides the library's layered defaults. */
.my-surface { --syn-accent: #a9f890; }
```

## Optional charts and microvisualizations

Load `syntyr.viz.css` after core for seven-theme chart colors, figure/legend
styling, inline SVG sparklines, bar lists, status trackers and heatmap cells.
Syntyr only styles supplied HTML/SVG; it does not create chart geometry,
fetch data or require a renderer. Read [Syntyr Viz](viz.md) and open the
[static seven-theme gallery](../examples/viz.html).

## Accessibility and performance contracts

- Actual semantic HTML and associated labels; use `button` for actions and `a` for navigation.
- Visible `:focus-visible` outline; do not remove it with theme overrides.
- Contrast target: WCAG 2.2 AA for text; manually verify any customized tokens.
- Honor user preferences: `prefers-reduced-motion`, `forced-colors`; effects opt-in and static.
- Avoid relying on color alone for state; use labels or icons with text alternatives.
- Raw/gzip bundle sizes are reported by `python3 scripts/asset_report.py`, with no hard size ceilings; runtime JS: 0 bytes.
- Browser coverage: current Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. The included automated browser suite runs Chromium when installed and can be extended to other engines.
- Do not automatically treat the demo or contract tests as an accessibility certification: test screen readers, 200%/400% zoom, form errors, contrast, and actual products separately.

## Distribution behavior

The repository now includes an **optional CSS-only `package.json` for package-manager distribution**; there is still no Node runtime requirement, bundling dependency, or mandatory package manager. A standard Python 3 build script creates deterministic concatenated CSS and validates exact committed outputs (see [optional package-manager guide](package-managers.md)):

```sh
python3 scripts/build.py
python3 scripts/build.py --check
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

## Licensing and provenance

MIT; this version is original work, not a fork or copy of Pico CSS, Chota or Open Props. If future work ports code from an upstream library, preserve that project's copyright and MIT notices and document the relevant files in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.


## Embedded versus full-page usage

`syn-root` provides a bounded styling context. Add `syn-page` **only for full-page experiences**. This separation prevents an embedded themed widget from unexpectedly forcing a viewport-height section.

```html
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="noir">
  <div class="syn-panel">This can be embedded inside an existing application.</div>
</section>
```

For invalid form controls, associate error text through native labeling and `aria-describedby`, and set `aria-invalid="true"` for server-provided errors. `syn-error` changes text color; do not rely on color alone to communicate invalid state.

```html
<label class="syn-label" for="email">Email</label>
<input class="syn-input" id="email" type="email" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="email-error">
<p class="syn-error" id="email-error">Enter a valid email address.</p>
```

## v0.3 compositional patterns (no build step)

The following are ordinary CSS classes in `syntyr.core.css`:

| Class | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.syn-region` | Named `syn-region` inline-size container for independent widget responsiveness |
| `.syn-split` | Stacked by default; two columns at container width >=43rem |
| `.syn-stats` | One/two/three columns at container widths <31rem, >=31rem, >=55rem |
| `.syn-stat`, `.syn-stat-label`, `.syn-stat-value` | Semantic telemetry card presentation |
| `.syn-empty` | Centered dashed-outline empty-state composition |
| `.syn-pricing`, `.syn-price-card` | One column until 43rem, then three equal columns |
| `.syn-price-card[data-syn-featured]` | Opt-in highlighted plan, purely visual, no ARIA claim |
| `.syn-price-value`, `.syn-feature-list` | Pricing typography and list styles |
| `.syn-toolbar` | Wrapping flex toolbar |

Attach `.syn-region` **on an ancestor** of the patterns. A region element isn't its own query container descendant; without a region ancestor the patterns remain readable one-column layouts. Nest separate regions for independently sized widgets. The `syn-region` name prevents unrelated page containers from changing their layouts.

Button state: `.syn-button[aria-pressed="true"]` is a pressed **toggle button**; `[data-syn-state="active"]` is decoration/host state; `[aria-busy="true"]` expresses in-progress updates but does not actually disable interactions. State changes and form handling are application responsibilities.

Additional inherited tokens: `--syn-ease`, `--syn-duration-fast`, `--syn-success`, `--syn-warning`. Extend themes with unlayered `.syn-root[data-syn-theme="custom"] { --syn-accent: ... }` CSS. Test contrast for your own values.

See [theme customization and token overrides](theme-customization.md), [MIT composition recipes](recipes.md) and [Tailwind architectural research](tailwind-research.md).

## Optional SaaS, business and CLI compositions (development branch)

Load `syntyr.core.css` first and `syntyr.recipes.css` second. The core remains separate from optional recipes; measure each bundle instead of enforcing a fixed byte cap.

| Context | Optional classes |
| --- | --- |
| SaaS | `.syn-app-shell`, `.syn-app-rail`, `.syn-app-nav`, `.syn-workspace`, `.syn-app-topbar`, `.syn-kpi-grid`, `.syn-app-card`, `.syn-activity-list` |
| Business website | `.syn-site-hero`, `.syn-site-heading`, `.syn-feature-grid`, `.syn-feature-card`, `.syn-cta-band` |
| Browser terminal | `.syn-terminal`, `.syn-terminal-bar`, `.syn-terminal-body`, `.syn-terminal-line`, `.syn-terminal-prompt` |
| Surface design | `.syn-frame--precision`, `.syn-frame--industrial`, `.syn-frame--soft` |

Native disabled buttons cannot activate; aria-disabled does not block activation by itself. Host application code must suppress actions when ARIA-disabled and should preserve focus when appropriate. Syntyr does not disable click handlers via CSS.

Professional light mode: `data-syn-theme="studio"`. Colors and geometry are intentionally independent. Use `.syn-table-emphasis` for explicit cell highlighting instead of relying on last-column position; `.syn-status--success`, `--warning`, or `--danger` should always accompany readable status text.

Native terminal applications cannot render CSS. Use `terminal/palettes.json` as the portable color reference. See [usage and accessibility guidance](saas-cli-business.md). For bevel, notch, bracket, inset and circuit frame geometry, load the optional geometry stylesheet and follow [the frame guide](geometry-terminal.md). All new visual classes are optional and require no runtime JavaScript.


## Minimalist compositions (experimental)

`syntyr.recipes.css` also includes `.syn-sidebar` (two-column intrinsic
sidebar/content), `.syn-switcher` (all-or-nothing responsive card row),
fluid typography utilities `.syn-fluid-display` / `.syn-fluid-lede`,
and `.syn-reading`. These are not part of `syntyr.core.css`.
Classless checkbox and radio labels align their controls inline when
`syntyr.semantic.css` and `.syn-semantic` are enabled. See
[the recipe guide](recipes.md) and [live example](../examples/minimalist-patterns.html).

## Visual role examples

The optional [design-state example](../examples/design-states.html) exercises active, selected, disabled, and invalid presentation across nested light/dark themes. It contains no application state machine, backend operation, or runtime JavaScript.

## Progressive rendering extensions

System-aware `data-syn-theme="auto"` is built into core CSS. Use optional
`syntyr.print.css` for printable reports and the
[progressive-enhancement guide](progressive-enhancement.md) for fallbacks.

## Source: docs/recipes.md

# MIT-licensed composition recipes

For copyable input groups, labeled fields, container-responsive settings forms and optional headless UI styling, see [form composition recipes](component-recipes.md) and the [Radix adapter](radix-integration.md).

These original Syntyr recipes are free to copy, edit, commercialize, and distribute under MIT. No Tailwind Plus source or premium assets were copied. For live examples see [the gallery](index.html), the [Grid console](../examples/console.html), and the [Noir pricing layout](../examples/pricing.html).

## 1. Responsive telemetry cards

The `.syn-region` element establishes a **named inline-size container**. Unlike media queries, the cards respond to the width of the enclosing widget/sidebar. This is a native browser feature; no JavaScript observer is needed.

```html
<section class="syn-root syn-region" data-syn-theme="grid" aria-label="Network telemetry">
  <div class="syn-stats">
    <article class="syn-stat"><span class="syn-stat-label">UPTIME</span><p class="syn-stat-value">99.8%</p></article>
    <article class="syn-stat"><span class="syn-stat-label">NODES</span><p class="syn-stat-value">24</p></article>
    <article class="syn-stat"><span class="syn-stat-label">ALERTS</span><p class="syn-stat-value">02</p></article>
  </div>
</section>
```

## 2. Accessible empty state

```html
<section class="syn-empty" aria-labelledby="empty-heading">
  <p class="syn-eyebrow">QUEUE / EMPTY</p>
  <h2 id="empty-heading">No pending actions</h2>
  <p class="syn-muted">New items appear here once submitted.</p>
  <a class="syn-button syn-button--primary" href="/new">Create an item</a>
</section>
```

This is a *visual composition*, not a live queue implementation. Preserve real links, meaningful labels, and server-side behavior.

## 3. Three-card pricing display

```html
<section class="syn-root syn-region" data-syn-theme="noir" aria-label="Illustrative plans">
  <div class="syn-pricing">
    <article class="syn-price-card">
      <h2>Personal</h2>
      <p class="syn-price-value">$19<small> / month</small></p>
      <ul class="syn-feature-list"><li>One project</li><li>Basic support</li></ul>
      <a class="syn-button" href="/contact">Contact us</a>
    </article>
    <article class="syn-price-card" data-syn-featured>
      <h2>Studio</h2>
      <p class="syn-price-value">$49<small> / month</small></p>
      <ul class="syn-feature-list"><li>Unlimited projects</li><li>Team seats</li></ul>
      <a class="syn-button syn-button--primary" href="/contact">Contact us</a>
    </article>
    <article class="syn-price-card">
      <h2>Enterprise</h2>
      <p class="syn-price-value">Custom</p>
      <ul class="syn-feature-list"><li>Security review</li><li>Dedicated support</li></ul>
      <a class="syn-button" href="/contact">Contact us</a>
    </article>
  </div>
</section>
```

## 4. Stateful native button (host controlled)

```html
<button type="button" class="syn-button" aria-pressed="true">Grid view</button>
<button type="button" class="syn-button" aria-busy="true">Syncing status</button>
```

`aria-pressed="true"` conveys a real toggle state to accessibility APIs; set it only when a toggle actually is pressed. `aria-busy` signals that updates are in progress; it **does not** disable a button or create loading logic. The UI state must come from your application/server. If a state is only decorative, use `data-syn-state="active"` instead of misusing ARIA.

## Token-only custom theme

```css
/* Unlayered application CSS intentionally overrides Syntyr's layered tokens. */
.syn-root[data-syn-theme="custom"] {
  --syn-bg: #0b1019;
  --syn-surface: #192333;
  --syn-accent: #82f9d1;
  --syn-on-accent: #09120e;
  --syn-text: #eefbf7;
  --syn-muted: #bbd4ce;
  --syn-frame: #496b68;
}
```

For custom themes, test *every* textual token pairing and important state for WCAG contrast. The example overrides only a subset of the available color tokens and is not an accessibility certification.

## Reusing recipes across stacks

- **Go / templ, PHP, Django, Rust templates:** Make recipes server-rendered partials and pass content as arguments.
- **HTMX / Datastar:** Use the same classes on server-returned fragments. Their JavaScript, if chosen, is outside the CSS library.
- **React / Vue / Astro:** Wrap the exact markup in framework components only when the host application calls for it.

Favor stable component classes and CSS variables over copying long lists of generated utilities. See [contract](components.md) and [Tailwind research](tailwind-research.md).

## Accessible navigation and loading placeholders

Breadcrumbs use a real ordered list inside a labeled navigation landmark. The separator is a CSS border rather than spoken punctuation:

```html
<nav class="syn-breadcrumbs" aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  <ol>
    <li><a href="/">Home</a></li>
    <li><span aria-current="page">Reports</span></li>
  </ol>
</nav>
```

Page controls are **real links**, not inert buttons. Match the selected page to the actual URL, and label any symbol-only links:

```html
<nav class="syn-pagination" aria-label="Results pages">
  <a class="syn-page-link" href="?page=1">1</a>
  <a class="syn-page-link" href="?page=2" aria-current="page">2</a>
  <a class="syn-page-link" href="?page=3">3</a>
</nav>
```

Skeletons are deliberately static. Hide the visual placeholder from assistive technology and announce loading outside it with application-owned state. Do not leave an infinite loading message or use fake progress values:

```html
<section aria-busy="true" aria-label="Reports">
  <p role="status">Loading reports…</p>
  <span class="syn-skeleton" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span class="syn-skeleton syn-skeleton--short" aria-hidden="true"></span>
</section>
```

When loading finishes, the application replaces the placeholders with content and clears `aria-busy`. The CSS library does not implement fetching or state changes.

## Server-rendered SaaS filter and settings patterns

The [SaaS workflow demonstration](../examples/saas-workflows.html) shows how to combine standard HTML search forms, a table, navigation landmarks, native settings disclosures and no-JavaScript placeholders. The page's data is illustrative and **is not filtered**; the following behavior belongs to the host application:

- Parse and validate `query`, `status`, `owner` and `page` on the server, apply authorization before filtering, paginate the results, and escape all rendered user input.
- Preserve submitted form values and `aria-current` based on the actual result page, and emit a truthful result count plus empty-state or error message.
- Persist preferences in the server's settings endpoint, with CSRF protection for changes; the static demo intentionally has no save button.
- When using HTMX, Datastar or another enhancement layer, keep GET filters, ordinary links and form labels working without client-side JavaScript.

The scoped `examples/saas-workflows.css` stylesheet contains layout glue only and is **not** added to the distributed core or all-in-one bundle.


## Intrinsic responsive layouts (optional recipes CSS)

Load `syntyr.core.css` plus `syntyr.recipes.css`. The layout primitives are
scoped to `.syn-root` and require no JavaScript, framework or viewport media
queries. Their children are ordinary semantic HTML.

```html
<section class="syn-root">
  <div class="syn-sidebar" style="--syn-sidebar-width: 14rem">
    <aside>Navigation or filters</aside>
    <main>Main content</main>
  </div>
  <div class="syn-switcher" style="--syn-switcher-threshold: 42rem">
    <article>First card</article>
    <article>Second card</article>
    <article>Third card</article>
  </div>
</section>
```

`.syn-sidebar` expects **exactly two** direct children: sidebar first,
content second. Defaults: sidebar 16rem, content minimum 28rem (capped at
100% of available width). In narrow containers they stack, and neither
child is forced wider than the container by the layout primitive. Content
with long unbreakable text should still use appropriate wrapping.

`.syn-switcher` treats all direct children uniformly. Above the 40rem
default threshold they share a row; below it every child stacks. Override
`--syn-switcher-threshold` per instance. This differs from `.syn-grid`,
which can display different numbers of columns at intermediate widths.

Use opt-in fluid type classes `.syn-fluid-display`, `.syn-fluid-lede` and
`.syn-reading`. The CSS custom properties `--syn-fluid-display-size`,
`--syn-type-lede` and `--syn-reading-width` can be overridden in plain
application CSS. Keep real document headings and reading order.

See [the working minimalist demo](../examples/minimalist-patterns.html).

---

## Source: docs/component-recipes.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/component-recipes.md

# Copy-owned form recipes

These are **MIT-licensed, plain-HTML examples**. Copy and modify them without installing a Syntyr CLI, template registry, React, or a JavaScript runtime. Syntyr provides presentation; your browser and application provide behavior.

Load `dist/syntyr.core.css` and apply `.syn-root` on a stable ancestor. Input groups and fields are included in core. The examples below also work in Go/templ, Askama, Django templates, Astro, React, and HTMX.

## 1. Labeled field with assistance and server-side validation

```html
<div class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <div class="syn-field">
    <label class="syn-label" for="email">Work email</label>
    <input class="syn-input" id="email" name="email" type="email"
           autocomplete="email" aria-invalid="true"
           aria-describedby="email-help email-error" required>
    <p class="syn-help" id="email-help">Use your company email address.</p>
    <p class="syn-error" id="email-error">Enter a valid work email.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

Only render `aria-invalid="true"` and the error message when the form is actually invalid. Do not use CSS as a substitute for server-side validation. The field class groups presentation; the native `label for` association supplies the accessible name.

## 2. Search field with a connected button

```html
<search class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio" aria-label="Search accounts">
  <form method="get" action="/accounts">
    <div class="syn-field">
      <label class="syn-label" for="account-query">Account name</label>
      <div class="syn-input-group">
        <input class="syn-input" id="account-query" name="q"
               type="search" placeholder="Search accounts">
        <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary" type="submit">Search</button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </form>
</search>
```

This is **progressive enhancement**: the GET form submits with **No JavaScript**. An HTMX application may add `hx-get` and `hx-target` while preserving `action`, `method`, and a server-rendered fallback. The application must implement the endpoint and return actual search results.

## 3. Input addon (currency and unit)

```html
<div class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <div class="syn-field">
    <label class="syn-label" for="monthly-budget">Monthly budget (USD)</label>
    <div class="syn-input-group">
      <span class="syn-input-addon" aria-hidden="true">$</span>
      <input class="syn-input" id="monthly-budget" name="budget"
             type="number" min="0" step="0.01" inputmode="decimal">
      <span class="syn-input-addon" aria-hidden="true">USD</span>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

The unit is included in the label, not only in the decorative addon; assistive technologies must not depend on a symbol alone. Keep addons concise; overly long addons can compress their associated input.

## 4. Container-responsive horizontal form

```html
<form class="syn-root syn-region syn-form" action="/settings" method="post"
      data-syn-theme="corporate">
  <div class="syn-field-row">
    <label class="syn-label" for="org-name">Organization</label>
    <div class="syn-field-body">
      <input class="syn-input" id="org-name" name="organization"
             aria-describedby="org-help" required>
      <p class="syn-help" id="org-help">Visible to members of your team.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary" type="submit">Save</button>
</form>
```

The `syn-region` container determines whether rows become horizontal at 42rem. Without that ancestor they remain safely stacked. This is intentionally not a full grid/breakpoint framework. The help text is associated with its input via `aria-describedby`. A production POST endpoint must handle authorization, validation and CSRF.

## Optional companion styles

- [Radix Primitives state styling](radix-integration.md) provides an opt-in adapter for React applications while keeping Radix responsible for keyboard behavior.
- shadcn/ui components can adopt Syntyr tokens in application-owned CSS. Modern color variables can use values such as `--background: var(--syn-bg)` and `--foreground: var(--syn-text)`, **only when** the shadcn component expects complete CSS color values. Older `hsl(var(--background))` consumers require an HSL-channel bridge instead; do not apply the mappings blindly.
- `syntyr.semantic.css` remains a separate opt-in style for unclassed native HTML. Do not apply it indiscriminately around other component libraries.

See [the static form showcase](../examples/form-composition.html) and the [main component contract](components.md).

## Source: docs/mature-system-patterns.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/mature-system-patterns.md

# Mature design-system patterns in Syntyr

These opt-in, CSS-only styles adapt lessons from established design systems without copying their source code or adding a JavaScript runtime dependency. See the [static example](../examples/mature-patterns.html).

## Why these patterns?

| System | Verified lesson | Syntyr response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Bootstrap](https://getbootstrap.com/docs/5.3/forms/validation/) | Do not rely on inaccessible custom validation tooltips; associate server-side messages with controls | Keep native form validation; style `aria-invalid` controls and a visible, linkable error summary |
| [GOV.UK](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/error-summary/) | A page-level summary should link to each invalid field and match its local error message | `.syn-error-summary` is presentation-only; use it alongside `.syn-error` |
| [GOV.UK summary list](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/summary-list/) | Key/value reviews benefit from native `dl`, `dt`, `dd` semantics and explicit action labels | `.syn-description-list` adapts to a named container and logical text direction |
| [Carbon](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/data-table/accessibility) | Sorting must be keyboard-operable and programmatically exposed | `.syn-table th[aria-sort]` provides styling for a real application-owned `button`, never fake sorting |
| [Tailwind](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/theme/) / [Open Props](https://open-props.style/) | Small reusable tokens and predictable compositions are more valuable than duplicate variants | Reuse existing `--syn-*` variables rather than inventing another token model |

## Server-rendered error handling

1. Keep the submitted field values and preserve the input's `name` and `id`.
2. On validation errors, render a page-level `.syn-error-summary` with a heading (for example `There is a problem`) and a list of anchors pointing to each erroneous input ID.
3. Beside each affected field, render the same actionable message in `.syn-error`, set `aria-invalid="true"`, and reference the error ID with `aria-describedby` along with any hint IDs.
4. After a failed submission, **move focus to the summary** with application/server framework logic. A `tabindex="-1"` makes it programmatically focusable but does **not** focus it on its own. A server-rendered page can provide an explicit navigation/focus strategy as appropriate to its stack.
5. Do not enable custom JavaScript validation tooltips. Browser-native validation is preferable unless the application deliberately implements a tested validation flow. If using `novalidate`, the server must actually validate; CSS cannot validate inputs.

Example (the action and value originate in the host application):

```html
<div class="syn-error-summary" role="alert" tabindex="-1"
     aria-labelledby="error-heading">
  <h2 id="error-heading">There is a problem</h2>
  <ul><li><a href="#email">Enter an email address</a></li></ul>
</div>
<label class="syn-label" for="email">Email</label>
<p class="syn-error" id="email-error">Error: Enter an email address</p>
<input class="syn-input" id="email" name="email" type="email"
       aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="email-error">
```

Avoid re-announcing the same error multiple times through nested live regions. Test the actual form flow with NVDA/VoiceOver and keyboard users; using `role="alert"` does not guarantee consistent announcements when the entire document loads. The example is server-rendered markup, not an implementation of validation or focus movement.

## Description lists for review screens

Use `dl` for key/value pairs, not a visual-only grid of `div` elements. A row uses a direct `div` child, then `dt` and one or more `dd` children. An optional `dd.syn-description-actions` holds an action with a specific, self-descriptive accessible name such as "Change account name".

The layout defaults to one column. Wrap in an ancestor `.syn-region` to enable a three-column layout at a container width of 38rem or more. The last column can be empty when there is no action; it never changes the DOM reading order. Use native `dir="rtl"` and `lang` as appropriate to the content.

## Sortable tables

The `aria-sort` attribute belongs on **one** active column's `th`, with the value `ascending` or `descending` as appropriate. Use a real `button type="button"` inside the header for keyboard access. On activation the **application** must reorder rows and update `aria-sort` consistently; Syntyr only supplies the affordance and arrow glyph, never sorting behavior.

Leave inactive column headers without `aria-sort` or explicitly use `none` when a button is present. Prefer `scope="col"`, a caption/accessible table name and useful row headers. Place wide tables in a `.syn-table-wrap` region with an accessible name and keyboard focus when overflow makes the region scrollable.

## RTL, forced-colors and reliability

The new compositions use logical border/padding properties. Table base alignment uses `text-align: start` and numeric cells use `text-align: end` rather than hard-coded left/right alignment, so they follow the active writing direction.

Navigation and geometry also honor the nearest `dir` context: `.syn-app-nav` places its active marker at the inline start, breadcrumb separators mirror, `.syn-panel--cut` places its clipped corner at the inline end, and the asymmetric `.syn-frame--notch` and `.syn-frame--circuit` decorations mirror without reversing the text itself. A nested `dir="ltr"` subsection remains LTR even inside an RTL parent. These visual rules use native `:dir(rtl)`, not a new theme or JavaScript.

This is a **targeted RTL improvement**, not a claim that every Syntyr recipe, animation, third-party integration or mixed writing mode has received a complete human localization audit.

Test in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit at desktop/mobile widths, 200% and 400% browser zoom, keyboard-only navigation, real screen readers, and operating-system forced-colors mode before declaring release readiness. The existing `@media (forced-colors: active)` fallback makes error-summary borders visible with system colors, but cannot substitute for human checks.

All styles work with a local copy of `syntyr.core.css`. No JavaScript, framework dependency or new theme tokens are necessary.

---

## Source: docs/radix-integration.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/radix-integration.md

# Optional Radix Primitives visual adapter

Syntyr core remains plain CSS with zero runtime JavaScript and zero React dependencies. Radix is a **separate application choice**. Its components own the accessible name, **ARIA** attributes, focus management, keyboard controls and state updates. Syntyr only adds styling.

## Install and opt in

In a React project using Radix Primitives, add a link **after** the core CSS:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/radix/states.css">
```

Copy [the adapter](../integrations/radix/states.css) into your project, or reference its repository source. Do not load it when you do not use Radix. It is **not** included in `syntyr.all.css`, either.

Wrap the relevant app area in `.syn-root`. Apply `.syn-radix` on that root, on a container inside it, **or directly on a stateful Syntyr control** to opt in only that control. If Radix portals content to the document body, set that portal's `container` inside the styled root, or style the portal explicitly. Do not assume portal content inherits Syntyr tokens when it is mounted outside the root.

## Example: controlled behavior, CSS presentation

```jsx
import * as Accordion from "@radix-ui/react-accordion";
import * as Toggle from "@radix-ui/react-toggle";

export function Controls() {
  return (
    <section className="syn-root syn-radix" data-syn-theme="studio">
      <Toggle.Root className="syn-button" aria-label="Pin dashboard">
        Pin dashboard
      </Toggle.Root>
      <Accordion.Root type="single" collapsible>
        <Accordion.Item value="filters">
          <Accordion.Header>
            <Accordion.Trigger className="syn-button syn-accordion-trigger">
              Advanced filters
            </Accordion.Trigger>
          </Accordion.Header>
          <Accordion.Content className="syn-accordion-content">
            <p>Additional filters belong here.</p>
          </Accordion.Content>
        </Accordion.Item>
      </Accordion.Root>
    </section>
  );
}
```

Radix supplies `data-state="on"`, `data-state="open"`, `data-state="closed"`, and `data-disabled` where applicable. The adapter consumes only those documented state hooks on **explicit Syntyr component classes**. It does not create a generic `data-state` styling API, and it does not replace Radix behavior.

## Accessibility and compatibility boundaries

- Test with keyboard only (Enter, Space, Arrow keys where appropriate, Escape) and screen readers; CSS passing a contract test is **not** an accessibility certification.
- Use a native button or Radix trigger for actions. Visual `[data-disabled]` states do not prevent click handlers from running; Radix/application logic must enforce disabled behavior.
- Preserve the focus-visible indication from Syntyr core and verify contrasts for all themes and custom token overrides.
- Avoid CSS-only emulations of focus traps, listbox navigation, complex comboboxes or dialogs.
- The adapter does not guarantee complete styling for every Radix primitive. Extend it with component-specific classes only when real use cases justify maintenance.

Related: [copy-owned component recipes](component-recipes.md), [framework integrations](framework-integrations.md).

## Source: docs/distribution.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/distribution.md

# Syntyr CSS distribution

Syntyr CSS is MIT-licensed. No NPM install, JavaScript runtime, fonts,
icons, Sass compiler or CSS framework is required to use the distributed CSS.

## Recommended: self-host a versioned stylesheet

1. Download the asset from the [GitHub release](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/releases/tag/v0.3.0-alpha.4), or copy the matching file from the tag.
2. Put `syntyr.core.css` in your application's static CSS directory.
3. Load it normally:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="grid">
  <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary">Initialize</button>
</section>
```

The stylesheet's path is *your* path; mount or copy the file there.
The above works with Go templates, plain HTML, Astro, HTMX, React and other
renderers. See [the framework integration guide](framework-integrations.md) for
HTMX request-state classes, optional semantic markers, and server-side fragments. Add `syn-page` to the root only if you want full-page min-height.

## Optional npm/package-manager distribution

A CSS-only `@syntyr/css` manifest is available in the alpha.5 repository candidate, but **it has not been published to npm**. See [package-manager installation and local tarball testing](package-managers.md) for supported imports and an explicit no-publication boundary. No package manager is required for the documented self-hosted stylesheet path.

## Optional themes and semantic HTML

Grid, Noir and Studio ship in the **same** core stylesheet; set
`data-syn-theme="grid"` or `data-syn-theme="noir"` or `data-syn-theme="studio"` on the scoped root.
You can nest differently themed elements.

The unreleased alpha.5 candidate adds Industrial, Terminal, Corporate and Minimal using the same scoped `data-syn-theme` contract. The published alpha.4 release includes Grid, Noir and Studio only.

Load `syntyr.semantic.css` after core **only** if you want automatic semantic
element styles within `.syn-semantic`. For static glows and decorative grid
effects, load `syntyr.effects.css` after core. SaaS, business and terminal layouts
are opt-in via `syntyr.recipes.css`. Optional frame geometry is in `syntyr.geometry.css`.
The alpha.5 working tree additionally provides `syntyr.utilities.css` for finite
layout helpers and `syntyr.print.css` for print-friendly reports. System-aware
Grid/Studio `data-syn-theme="auto"` is already included in core CSS, with
no additional stylesheet or runtime JavaScript. See the
[progressive-enhancement guide](progressive-enhancement.md) for examples.
The optional `syntyr.symbols.css` adds BYO-SVG icon sizing, literal Unicode styling and ASCII/box-drawing alignment without shipping fonts or icons; see [symbols and accessibility](symbols.md).

`syntyr.css` bundles core and effects. `syntyr.all.css` bundles all modules
while still requiring `.syn-semantic` to opt into semantic element styles.
Avoid loading these bundles alongside their component files: that duplicates CSS. Optional utilities live in the final `syn.utilities` cascade layer, allowing explicitly applied utility classes to override ordinary component declarations; see [the architecture policy](../ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Optional explicit selective build

Applications needing fewer core components can assemble a custom CSS file with
the Python standard-library-only `scripts/build_selective.py`. It does not scan
templates or purge individual selectors, and does not alter published assets.
See [selective builds and their limits](selective-builds.md).

## Pinned CDN for prototyping

```html
<link rel="stylesheet"
      href="https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/v/0.3.0-alpha.4/syntyr.core.css">
```

The first-party Cloudflare CDN serves frozen, checksum-verified CSS releases
from a global edge network. Unversioned `/dist/` URLs can change with builds;
pin `/v/<version>/` instead. The documentation's optional theme editor
has JavaScript, but the library CSS and consumer sites do not require it.
For production applications, copying the versioned CSS to your own origin
usually avoids an additional hostname connection.

## Release artifacts and guarantees

The published alpha.4 release contains seven SYNTYR CSS distributions. The
unreleased alpha.5 working tree currently contains ten SYNTYR distributions,
including the optional utilities, print and symbols stylesheets, plus
the terminal ANSI palette JSON, this guide, MIT license, and README. No retired compatibility aliases are shipped. The ZIP is created deterministically using only
Python's standard library:

```sh
python3 scripts/build.py --check
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python3 scripts/package_release.py
```

Both visual themes and all essential components are MIT-licensed. Commercial
premium templates, if introduced, will be independently authored and sold
separately. This v0.3 alpha is **not** a v1 production compatibility guarantee;
cross-browser and full accessibility audits are still release gates.

The `syn-` selectors, `--syn-` custom properties and `data-syn-` attributes are the only supported source API.

## Source: docs/api-stability.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/api-stability.md

# SYNTYR CSS public API and prerelease stability

**Status: experimental `0.3.0-alpha.5` candidate; no v1 stability promise.**
This document names the intended public contracts so that changes can be
reviewed consistently before `1.0.0`. It is not a new compatibility guarantee.

## Public surface and intended v1 boundaries

| Surface | Current policy | Intent for v1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `syntyr.core.css`, `.syn-root`, stable component classes | Public prerelease API | Stable selectors and behavior |
| New `.syn-field`, `.syn-field-row`, `.syn-field-body`, `.syn-input-group`, `.syn-input-addon` form compositions | Experimental prerelease core additions | Evaluate for v1 stabilization after browser/accessibility review |
| Documented `--syn-*` design-token names | Public prerelease API | Stable names, not fixed default values |
| `data-syn-theme` and documented `data-syn-*` state hooks | Public prerelease API | Stable names and meanings |
| `syntyr.semantic.css` and `.syn-semantic` | Opt-in prerelease API | Stable scoped semantics after audit |
| `syntyr.recipes.css`, `syntyr.geometry.css` | Experimental, opt-in | Evaluate for individual stabilization |
| `syntyr.effects.css`, `syntyr.utilities.css` | Experimental, opt-in | Evaluate for individual stabilization |
| `syntyr.css`, `syntyr.all.css` | Public convenience bundles | Maintain documented contents/meaning at v1 |
| `terminal/palettes.json` | Optional example/palette asset | Separate compatibility decision from CSS |
| `integrations/`, `examples/`, documentation editor | Non-core adapters/showcases | No automatic CSS-core stability promise |

The `syn-*` selector namespace, `--syn-*` properties and `data-syn-*` attributes
remain the only Syntyr-specific styling namespace. ARIA states such as
`aria-pressed`, `aria-busy`, `aria-invalid` and native HTML state remain governed
by web-platform semantics, not a separate Syntyr state machine.

Core classes do **not** require an application build pipeline. The opt-in
semantic mode only styles elements under `.syn-semantic` within `.syn-root`.
Themes set design tokens; component selectors should not fork per theme. The
finite utilities are explicit overrides in their own final `syn.utilities`
cascade layer. Do not load a convenience bundle and its component modules
simultaneously.

## Compatibility and version policy

- Before v1: breaking prerelease changes are possible; document them in the
  changelog. Do not maintain obsolete aliases solely for alpha compatibility.
- After v1: breaking changes to stabilized selector names, attribute meanings,
  documented file entrypoints and core component behavior require a major
  version. Additions can use minor releases; corrections use patch releases
  when semantically compatible.
- Values and appearance are not identical across patch versions. Accessibility
  fixes may adjust color, spacing, focus or contrast without renaming tokens.
- Custom, undocumented selectors and implementation variables are not a
  supported extension API. Use documented tokens and composition instead.
- Versioned `/v/<version>/` CDN assets remain byte-for-byte immutable; prefer
  self-hosting or pinning a version for production deployments.

## Pre-1.0 release checklist

1. Confirm which individual classes and tokens merit permanent compatibility.
2. Finish keyboard, screen-reader, browser zoom and contrast review; automated
   scans do not establish WCAG conformance.
3. Validate the supported browser/version matrix on realistic applications,
   including nested themes, CSS utilities and semantic opt-in behavior.
4. Publish versioned docs, a reproducible CSS distribution and a complete
   migration note if prerelease contracts change.

See [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../ARCHITECTURE.md) for feature-admission criteria,
layer ownership and dependency boundaries. Optional package integrations may
provide additional contracts but must never introduce a mandatory core
runtime dependency.

---

## Source: docs/framework-integrations.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/framework-integrations.md

# Syntyr CSS integration guide: HTMX and common frontend stacks

Syntyr is a **CSS presentation layer**, not a state manager, request client, or component runtime.
It has no JavaScript initialization, no required build tool, and no runtime dependency.
Every example uses the same `syn-` classes, CSS tokens and standard HTML.

## Choose one styling mode

1. **Explicit classes (recommended for apps):** load `syntyr.core.css`, use
   `.syn-root` on a stable ancestor, then `.syn-button`, `.syn-panel`, `.syn-input`, etc.
2. **Optional semantic HTML:** additionally load `syntyr.semantic.css` after core and
   add `.syn-semantic` to a scoped ancestor. Unclassed HTML receives semantic styles.
   For an element that an interaction framework will add classes to, opt it in once
   with `data-syn-semantic`. This preserves semantic styling while host-managed
   classes such as `htmx-request` are added and removed.

```html
<section class="syn-root syn-semantic" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <button data-syn-semantic hx-get="/status" hx-target="#status">Check status</button>
  <div id="status" aria-live="polite"></div>
</section>
```

**Host isolation:** Loading the CSS alone does not style a `.syn-button`,
`.syn-panel`, or other Syntyr class outside `.syn-root`. Existing host UI
components and CSS retain their presentation. Put `.syn-root` on the actual
Syntyr subtree (or on the component itself); do not assume a globally
scoped component class creates its own theme root. Syntyr uses native CSS
nesting for this boundary, so test embedding in each target browser.

The marker is only considered **inside** `.syn-semantic`, so it does not style
elements elsewhere. Do not put it on elements styled by a separate component
library unless you explicitly want Syntyr semantic styling there. Prefer
`.syn-button` for already-classed controls. The marker does **not** make the
control stateful, disabled, or accessible by itself.

## HTMX: progressive enhancement

A complete example with a real stdlib Python HTTP server is at:
[examples/htmx.html](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/examples/htmx.html),
[examples/htmx_server.py](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/examples/htmx_server.py), and
[examples/htmx.css](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/examples/htmx.css).
These links lead to source files, not a live Cloudflare demonstration.

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 examples/htmx_server.py
# open http://127.0.0.1:8765/examples/htmx.html
```

The optional demo loads **pinned HTMX 2.0.8** from a third-party CDN. The CSS
library doesn't load HTMX automatically. Production applications should
self-host the pinned HTMX asset for control over performance, integrity, and CSP.

The search form uses a real `action` and `method=get`. When HTMX sends
`HX-Request: true`, the server returns only the result fragment. Ordinary
navigation gets a complete HTML document. The server emits `Vary: HX-Request`
to keep caches from mixing the representations, and escapes user-controlled
query text before inserting it in HTML.

For best results:

- Put `.syn-root` and `data-syn-theme` **outside** the swapped element.
- Swap the narrowest stable target (normally `innerHTML` inside a results container).
- Give labels and inputs stable IDs; preserve native form submission as a fallback.
- Use the framework's `hx-indicator` and `hx-disabled-elt` when appropriate;
  `aria-busy` does **not** block duplicate submissions by itself.
- Do not create a permanent Syntyr HTMX runtime or register Syntyr lifecycle events.
- For strict CSP, use `includeIndicatorStyles: false` and an external stylesheet.
  The demo shows this pattern with a small **application-owned** `htmx.css`.
- Test initial document, request state, swapped fragment, form fallback, and
  failure paths in an actual browser.

The demo server intentionally exposes only four static assets and one GET route,
listens on localhost, and is **not** included in the Cloudflare static-site build.
A static host cannot serve its dynamic search endpoint without a backend.

## Alpine.js

Use native attributes for real state, and Syntyr classes for presentation:

```html
<div class="syn-root" x-data="{ selected: false }">
  <button class="syn-button" type="button"
          :aria-pressed="String(selected)" @click="selected = !selected">
    Toggle details
  </button>
</div>
```

Mount Alpine once in the host app. For `x-cloak`, define a tiny application
rule `[x-cloak] { display: none !important; }` before Alpine initializes.
Syntyr doesn't manage Alpine state.

## Datastar

Bind standard `aria-*`, `data-syn-state`, and class attributes to Datastar
signals. Style the resulting HTML as ordinary DOM. Keep the Syntyr theme root
outside morph targets, and let Datastar own request and signal behavior.
No Syntyr Datastar plugin is needed.

## React / Next.js

```jsx
import "./syntyr.core.css";

export function StatusCard({ status }) {
  return (
    <section className="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
      <article className="syn-panel">
        <h2 className="syn-heading">Operations</h2>
        <p>{status}</p>
      </article>
    </section>
  );
}
```

Import CSS once from the app entry point (or root layout, as supported by
the framework). No Syntyr provider, hooks, hydration, or dependency on React.

## Vue / Nuxt and Svelte / SvelteKit

Import the same CSS once. Bind native classes, `aria-*`, and
`data-syn-state` using each framework's built-in template syntax.
Do not wrap simple visual classes in additional runtime components unless the
application benefits from reusable semantic component boundaries.

## Astro, Hugo, Zola, Django, Rails, Go/templ and Rust templates

Serve `syntyr.core.css` as a normal static asset. Write HTML partials
with real headings, forms and links. Optional interactive islands can use
HTMX, Alpine, Datastar, React or native browser elements without changing
Syntyr's HTML/CSS contract. In Rails, Hotwire/Turbo updates have the same
theme-root and swap-boundary considerations as HTMX.

## Existing Tailwind or component-library applications

- Syntyr's `.syn-root` scope and `@layer syn.*` layers limit unintended
  interference, but Tailwind Preflight can still change global element defaults.
- Prefer explicit Syntyr classes. Apply `.syn-semantic` only to designated
  regions, not to a whole React/Headless UI component tree.
- Override public `--syn-*` tokens in application CSS; avoid copying or
  rebuilding utility frameworks inside Syntyr.
- Test cascade ordering, focus rings, dark/light color schemes, zoom and
  third-party components after integration.

## Performance and compatibility contract

- CSS bytes are tracked by `python3 scripts/asset_report.py` with optional JSON baseline comparisons; no arbitrary gzip release gate.
- Syntyr runtime JS: **zero**. HTMX/Alpine/React are host-app dependencies.
- Self-host assets on the app's own origin when practical; pin external CDN
  versions. Don't load both `syntyr.all.css` and its constituent stylesheets.
- Use Playwright or equivalent browser automation to verify dynamic class
  changes, HTMX fragments, responsiveness and accessibility.
- Avoid large DOM swaps, expensive decorative effects on scrolling tables,
  and unnecessary hydration. Measure actual page LCP, CLS and INP.

## Source: docs/theme-customization.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/theme-customization.md

# Syntyr theme customization — copy, override, ship

Syntyr themes are **CSS custom properties**, not JavaScript configuration.
The MIT core already includes Grid and Noir palettes, responsive primitives,
accessible focus styling and semantic element options.

## 1. Choose a theme

Without a `data-syn-theme` attribute, `.syn-root` now uses Studio. Select Grid or Noir explicitly for technical/cinematic styles. This change is only in the unreleased alpha.5 candidate; version-pinned alpha.4 assets remain unchanged.

Load the published `syntyr.core.css` in your application and use regular HTML:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="grid">
  <article class="syn-panel syn-panel--cut">
    <h2 class="syn-heading">Sector status</h2>
    <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary">Open</button>
  </article>
  <aside data-syn-theme="noir" class="syn-panel">
    Nested Noir preview
  </aside>
</section>
```

Use `data-syn-theme="noir"` for warm amber. Native HTML features
such as `details`, `dialog` and `popover` don't need framework JavaScript.

## 2. Override tokens using application CSS

Syntyr declares its defaults in named cascade layers. App CSS without a
layer takes precedence over layered author rules regardless of selector specificity.
Load application overrides **after** the Syntyr stylesheet to reduce surprises:

```css
/* app.css: original tokens, not copied from existing entertainment IP. */
.syn-root[data-syn-theme="grid"] {
  --syn-accent: #80dfef;
  --syn-on-accent: #07121a;
  --syn-accent-soft: rgb(128 223 239 / 10%);
  --syn-frame: #34576c;
}

/* Override one nested region without affecting the rest of the site. */
.my-warning-panel {
  --syn-surface: #1b232d;
  --syn-warning: #ffe2aa;
}
```

Important: `--syn-accent` is the most visible token, but `--syn-on-accent`
is the contrasting **foreground on primary buttons**. Change both when
necessary. Verify 4.5:1 contrast for body text and 3:1 for essential non-text
graphics; don't assume arbitrary overrides remain accessible.

Useful tokens:

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--syn-bg` | Main background |
| `--syn-surface`, `--syn-surface-hi` | Cards and controls |
| `--syn-text`, `--syn-muted` | Main and secondary text |
| `--syn-accent`, `--syn-on-accent`, `--syn-accent-soft` | Brand accent, its foreground, soft fill |
| `--syn-frame`, `--syn-danger`, `--syn-success`, `--syn-warning` | Borders and status |
| `--syn-font`, `--syn-mono`, `--syn-font-ui`, `--syn-font-display` | Body, technical, control, and display typography |
| `--syn-type-xs`, `--syn-type-sm`, `--syn-type-base` | Typography sizes |
| `--syn-surface-recessed`, `--syn-surface-raised`, `--syn-border-subtle` | Derived surfaces and quiet separators |
| `--syn-text-subtle`, `--syn-border-default`, `--syn-border-hover`, `--syn-border-focus`, `--syn-focus-ring` | Semantic text, borders, and focus |
| `--syn-surface-interactive`, `--syn-surface-hover`, `--syn-surface-pressed` | Theme-aware interactive control states |
| `--syn-type-display`, `--syn-type-section`, `--syn-type-heading`, `--syn-type-body`, `--syn-leading-body`, `--syn-tracking-display` | Composable typography roles |
| `--syn-row-padding-block`, `--syn-card-padding`, `--syn-control-padding-block` | Density-aware spacing |
| `--syn-space-1` … `--syn-space-5` | Spacing |
| `--syn-cut`, `--syn-radius`, `--syn-control-height` | Geometry |
| `--syn-duration-fast`, `--syn-ease` | Optional transitions |
| `--syn-panel-padding`, `--syn-panel-radius`, `--syn-panel-border-width` | Local panel customization |
| `--syn-button-padding-inline`, `--syn-button-border-width` | Local button customization |

## 3. Independent visual intensity

Use `data-syn-intensity="quiet"` on a dense dashboard, the default `standard` for a balanced presentation, or `cinematic` on a limited hero region. Intensity controls only opt-in decoration in `syntyr.effects.css`; it does not alter palette, density, typography or control contrast. Nested regions can override an inherited value. See the [visual-intensity guide](visual-intensity.md) and [live comparison](../examples/intensity-geometry.html).

## 4. CSS component mode versus native semantic mode

Scoped component classes: `.syn-panel`, `.syn-button`, `.syn-table`.
They work with only `syntyr.core.css`.

For classless HTML resembling Pico CSS, load **both** files and opt in:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.semantic.css">
<div class="syn-root syn-semantic" data-syn-theme="noir">
  <article>
    <h2>Operator access</h2>
    <label for="operator">Operator ID</label>
    <input id="operator" name="operator" required>
    <button>Continue</button>
  </article>
</div>
```

Unclassed controls outside `.syn-semantic` are not restyled.
If you need glows or static grid effects, add `syntyr.effects.css`
as a third optional file. Don't load `syntyr.all.css` **and** its
individual component files at the same time.

## 5. Responsive applications and accessibility

Use `.syn-region` as the parent for container-responsive patterns such as
`.syn-stats`, `.syn-split`, `.syn-pricing`; width comes from the container,
not the whole viewport. Use `.syn-page` only for a full-page experience.

Syntyr honors `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Theme overrides
must not remove focus outlines, fake disabled states, or communicate state
only through color. Test keyboard navigation, 200%/400% browser zoom,
high-contrast/forced-colors, and relevant screen readers in the target app.

**No runtime JavaScript is required for styling.** Search, authentication,
live data, and server-side form handling are intentionally application
responsibilities; optional advanced widgets are outside the CSS core.

## Seven theme palettes (unreleased alpha.5 candidate)

The published alpha.4 tag offers Grid, Noir and Studio. This candidate adds Industrial, Terminal, Corporate and Minimal. Use the same HTML and change only the theme attribute:

- `data-syn-theme="grid"`
- `data-syn-theme="noir"`
- `data-syn-theme="studio"`
- `data-syn-theme="industrial"`
- `data-syn-theme="terminal"`
- `data-syn-theme="corporate"`
- `data-syn-theme="minimal"`

To use finite opt-in layout utilities, load `syntyr.utilities.css` after `syntyr.core.css` (or use the all bundle). Utilities include `.syn-u-flex`, `.syn-u-grid`, `.syn-u-between`, spacing helpers and a visually hidden helper. No compiler or runtime JavaScript is required.


## System palette, no JavaScript (experimental)

`data-syn-theme="auto"` on `.syn-root` or a nested themed region
uses Studio colors for light system preference and Grid colors for dark
system preference. It relies on native `color-scheme: light dark` and
CSS `light-dark()`, supported by current Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
Older engines that lack `light-dark()` retain the inherited/default
palette. No preference is stored or read by Syntyr.

```html
<body class="syn-root syn-page" data-syn-theme="auto">
  <section data-syn-theme="noir">This remains Noir regardless of OS theme.</section>
</body>
```

Explicit palettes are unchanged. For sensitive applications, test nested
themes, native form controls, and contrast in both OS preference modes.
## Typography, density, and quiet surfaces

Control and navigation text uses `--syn-font-ui`. Display headings use
`--syn-font-display`, while code and CLI regions retain `--syn-mono`.
Grid and Terminal choose monospace UI explicitly; Studio is the implicit default; light themes and Noir use
system sans-serif controls. Replace the font variables if a product has its
own typeface, without introducing required external fonts.

The `--syn-surface-recessed`, `--syn-surface-raised`, and
`--syn-border-subtle` tokens derive from the active theme palette and
recompute in nested themed regions. Strong borders remain available for
focus and essential controls. Avoid treating subtle separators as a substitute
for accessible non-text contrast where boundaries are required.

To opt into compact operational layouts:

```html
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="minimal" data-syn-density="compact">
  <table class="syn-table"><!-- ... semantic rows ... --></table>
</section>
```

Compact density reduces padding and control heights, **not font sizes**.
Use the default density for content-heavy business pages or touch-first forms.
For an optional editorial hero, combine `syn-site-heading--editorial` from
`syntyr.recipes.css` with `syn-gradient-wash` from `syntyr.effects.css`.
Both use local fonts and static CSS without runtime dependencies.


## Semantic roles, states, and content rhythm

Use `.syn-display` (also available as `.syn-title`), `.syn-section-heading` for section titles, `.syn-heading` for card headings,
`.syn-body`, `.syn-text-support`, and the opt-in `.syn-prose` content
container. Typography roles inherit theme fonts and allow applications to
override type scale without rewriting individual component selectors.

Semantic aliases are derived separately in each nested `data-syn-theme`
scope, so a Grid panel inside a Studio page retains Grid's own contrast and
control appearance. To override theme colors, prefer changing the primitive
palette (`--syn-accent`, `--syn-frame`, `--syn-surface`, etc.). Override a
semantic role only when the change is intentional and contrast has been checked.

Native `disabled`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-pressed`, `aria-busy`,
`:focus-visible`, and `:active` styles are presentation only. `aria-busy`
does not stop clicks or run a task. Use actual `disabled` for disabled form
controls; `aria-disabled` requires the application to suppress activation.
For errors, pair `aria-invalid="true"` with an associated error message
(`aria-describedby`); never rely on border color alone.

See [the live design-state example](../examples/design-states.html) for
semantic typography, nested themes, compact layout and form states.

## Source: docs/visual-intensity.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/visual-intensity.md

# Visual intensity and composable cyberpunk frames

SYNTYR separates **palette** (`data-syn-theme`), **decorative intensity**
(`data-syn-intensity`), **density** (`data-syn-density`) and optional geometry
(`.syn-frame` plus one shape). These are independent controls and do not load
JavaScript, fonts, sprites or third-party assets.

## Choose the right intensity

Use `data-syn-intensity` on `.syn-root` or any descendant element. It is
inherited, so a child can opt into a different intensity without switching
palette. Omitting the attribute is equivalent to `standard`.

| Value | Effects | Good for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `quiet` | Nearly invisible grids/washes; no visible glow/scanline overlay | Data-heavy SaaS, forms, accessibility-sensitive dashboards |
| `standard` | Existing effect strengths and opt-in behavior (default) | Marketing sites, documentation |
| `cinematic` | Stronger washes, luminous shadows and optional scanlines | Demos, editorial hero sections, limited promotional panels |

Intensity changes **only opt-in decorative effects** from
`syntyr.effects.css`. It does not change status colors, border contrast,
focus rings, typography, form affordances or any theme's underlying palette.
For zero decoration, simply do not load effects.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.effects.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.geometry.css">

<main class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="grid" data-syn-intensity="quiet">
  <article class="syn-panel syn-glow">
    <h2>Operational view</h2>
    <p>Quiet default for dense data.</p>
  </article>
  <section data-syn-intensity="cinematic">
    <article class="syn-panel syn-glow syn-frame syn-frame--bevel syn-frame--accent">
      <h2>Featured transmission</h2>
      <p>A localized visual accent without changing colors or density.</p>
    </article>
  </section>
</main>
```

For custom presets, override `--syn-grid-alpha`, `--syn-glow-alpha`,
`--syn-wash-alpha`, `--syn-wash-secondary-alpha`,
`--syn-horizon-alpha`, and `--syn-scanline-alpha` on a region.
Values are percentages used in color interpolation, not animation speed.
Cinematic does **not** animate automatically; use optional motion modules
separately and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Geometry that composes

The optional `syntyr.geometry.css` stylesheet supports five shapes:
`bevel`, `notch`, `bracket`, `inset` and `circuit`.
Use exactly one shape on `.syn-frame`, optionally adding
`.syn-frame--accent` for a stronger outline (2px accent-colored border).
The geometry layer explicitly resets pseudo-element dimensions and clipping
from earlier CSS layers, so `.syn-panel--cut` on the **same host** is safely
superseded by the selected frame geometry rather than corrupting it.

```html
<article class="syn-panel syn-panel--cut syn-frame syn-frame--notch syn-frame--accent">
  <h2>System status</h2>
  <p>The notch frame takes precedence over the simpler panel cut.</p>
</article>
```

`syn-frame--accent` is an *optional* style modifier, not an additional
shape. Set `--syn-frame-cut`, `--syn-frame-stroke`,
`--syn-frame-fill` or `--syn-frame-outline` on the host to customize
one frame. Avoid combining two shape modifiers.

**Remaining composability boundary:** both `syn-frame` geometry and the
older `syn-frame--precision` recipe own `::before`. Applying both
to the same host still supersedes the precision accent; nest separate
elements when both treatments are needed. Likewise, geometry intentionally
uses a transparent host background so gradients painted on the **host**
may spill into its cut corners. Apply complex host backgrounds on an inner
element, or set `--syn-frame-fill` to a solid value.

## Accessibility and performance

- Always keep readable status text; never communicate errors only by glow or color.
- In forced-colors mode, frames fall back to solid system borders and effects
  suppress nonessential backgrounds.
- Prefer `quiet` for long operational pages; reserve `cinematic` for a few
  deliberate accents. Measure paint and scrolling on actual devices.
- The library core does not require any script. The optional docs theme editor
  can preview intensity but is not shipped as an application dependency.
- Test with 200% and 400% zoom, keyboard input, forced colors and all three
  browser engines before relying on a theme in production.

See [live intensity comparison](../examples/intensity-geometry.html),
[advanced geometry](geometry-terminal.md) and
[theme customization](theme-customization.md).
